title: Home and Town

story.title: Kamola’s new flat
story.text: Last month, Kamola moved to a new **flat** in Tashkent. Before that, she lived in a big **house** with a **garden** in a village. | Her new flat is on the fifth floor of a **modern** building. It has two **bedrooms**, a **living room**, a small **kitchen** and a **bathroom**. Her favourite place is the **balcony** – she drinks her morning tea there. The flat isn’t very **spacious**, but it’s **cosy**. She doesn’t have much **furniture** yet – only a bed, a table and a big blue **sofa**. | Kamola likes her **neighbourhood**. There is a **park** **opposite** her building and a **supermarket** **next to** it. The metro is very **near**, so she isn’t **far from** her office. | There is one problem: the street is quite **noisy** in the evening, and the metro is always **crowded**. But her **neighbours** are very friendly – the old woman next door often brings her bread! | Kamola misses her **quiet** village a little, but she is happy in her new home.

answers: What is your favourite room? Why?
**My favourite room is** my bedroom **because** it’s quiet and **cosy**. I study there and listen to music. **For example**, every evening I read on my bed.
My dream home is a **spacious** house with a big **garden** and a swimming pool. It’s **near** the mountains but not **far from** the city.
speech: Hello! I’d like to tell you about my home. **I live in a** flat **in** the centre of Samarkand. **There are** three **rooms in my flat**: a living room, my parents’ bedroom and my bedroom. **My favourite room is** the kitchen **because** we eat and talk together there. **It’s small but cosy.** **There’s a** park **opposite my house**, and a supermarket **next to** it. **It takes** ten **minutes to get to** school on foot. **The best thing about my area is** the friendly neighbours. **One problem is that** the street is noisy at night. But I love my home!
